newsitem.title: GERMANY: German regional metal worker wage talks collapse.
newsitem.headline: German regional metal worker wage talks collapse.

text.p: German metal workers union IG Metall said on Tuesday that regional wage talks in North Rhine-Westphalia, which had been seen to be the key to a possible national deal, had collapsed.
"The talks have collapsed," union negotiator Harald Schartau told journalists after all-night discussions, adding this had likely been the last chance to hammer out a deal at the negotiating table.

Talks in the region, which is home to some of Germany's largest steel producers and 850,000 workers in the sector, began on Monday morning and were seen to possibly provide a pilot agreement for the industry as a whole after attempts to secure a nationwide deal failed last month.

Martin Kannegiesser, head negotiator for the employers, said the two sides had agreed on many issues, but disagreements about a new model which sought to link special payments to sickdays had caused the talks to collapse.
"Both sides had errected many barriers, we tried to do a slalom, but we fell down," he told journalists.
